title: ToolSQL: A Tool-Assisted Agent for SQL Verification and Refinement

problem.claim: Text-to-SQL systems need to identify and correct database mismatches in generated SQL queries.

gap.claim: Existing methods address execution errors but struggle with database mismatches that do not trigger execution exceptions.

contributions.claim: A tool-assisted agent framework uses a retriever and a detector to diagnose and correct SQL queries with database mismatches.
SpiderMismatch is a dataset constructed to reflect condition-mismatch problems in real-world scenarios.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present the tool-assisted agent framework and SpiderMismatch as proposed or newly introduced contributions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The model was evaluated on Spider and Spider-Realistic in few-shot settings.
The model outperformed baseline methods on SpiderMismatch.

narrative_sequence.summary: Recent Text-to-SQL methods use database-management-system feedback through LLMs.
These methods struggle with non-exception-producing database mismatches, including condition and stricter-constraint mismatches.
The paper proposes a tool-assisted agent with retriever and detector tools for SQL verification and refinement.
The paper introduces the SpiderMismatch dataset.
The authors report effectiveness on Spider and Spider-Realistic and superiority over baselines on SpiderMismatch.

source_observation.claim: Execution feedback alone may miss condition and constraint mismatches that do not raise exceptions.

interpretation.claim: Semantic verification should complement execution-based validation for real-world SQL generation.

application.claim: Use specialized retrieval and detection tools to inspect generated queries against database-specific semantic requirements.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported datasets and few-shot settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not report quantitative metrics or dataset sizes.
The abstract does not specify how the retriever and detector operate.
The abstract does not detail the baseline methods or few-shot configurations.
